title: Towards a Theory of Quantum Hyperstructures
content: Quantum logic combines two sharp propositions by one join, which exists whether or not the propositions can be tested together and which keeps no record of that difference. We define a quantum hyperstructure to be a multivalued composition on the orthogonal projectors of a complex Hilbert space. Given two projectors, the composition returns every projector that commutes with both and whose range lies in the sum of their ranges. Its value is the family of sharp propositions still jointly compatible with the pair and supported on the subspace the pair generates. Associativity fails in general, already for a commuting triple, and holds on every Boolean algebra of mutually commuting projectors. In finite dimension the family is classified by the joint eigenspaces of the two projectors and by the principal angles between their ranges. The same composition determines the projector order and the compatibility relation. It is not a hyper effect sum, and the poset of its commuting joins is not a quantum suplattice. The construction makes the indeterminacy of incompatible measurement a law of composition, rather than only a failure of distributivity.
